data.hypothesis: A persistent OpenMP team should avoid repeatedly creating a team across six dependent timesteps. Static worksharing over disjoint (z,y) rows keeps x contiguous; each worksharing loop's implicit barrier ensures the next timestep sees completed output. This trades fork/join overhead for six synchronization points and tests one implementation against the serial baseline; it does not establish a comparison with a per-step-team implementation before controller measurement.
data.notes: Initialization, buffer parity, and update bounds are preserved; only the interior is written during each step. The supplied serial baseline is correct and has a three-sample mean of 0.464905 s, but no candidate measurements or one-versus-four-core timing comparisons are available here. Correctness and native wall time, including initialization and overhead, remain for the controller to measure.
transformations: Replace the serial six-step sweep with one OpenMP team whose lifetime spans all timesteps.
Use static collapse(2) worksharing across interior z/y rows while retaining contiguous x traversal.
Rely on the implicit worksharing barrier between steps to preserve timestep dependencies and buffer parity.
